name: Autism spectrum disorder
summary: Differences in social communication and interaction, with restricted or repetitive patterns of behavior and interests, present from early development.

name: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder
summary: A persistent pattern of inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity that interferes with functioning across settings.

name: Specific learning disorder
summary: Ongoing difficulty learning reading, writing or math skills that is well below what is expected for age.

name: Tourette’s disorder
summary: Multiple motor tics and at least one vocal tic, beginning in childhood and lasting over a year.

name: Intellectual disability
summary: Limits in reasoning, learning and everyday adaptive skills that begin during development.

name: Schizophrenia
summary: A long-lasting disorder involving some mix of delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech or behavior, and reduced expression or motivation.

name: Schizoaffective disorder
summary: Psychotic symptoms occurring alongside a major mood episode, with psychosis also present without mood symptoms at times.

name: Schizophreniform disorder
summary: Schizophrenia-like symptoms lasting between one and six months.

name: Brief psychotic disorder
summary: A sudden psychotic episode lasting at least a day but under a month, followed by return to prior functioning.

name: Delusional disorder
summary: Fixed false beliefs lasting a month or more without the wider picture of schizophrenia.

name: Bipolar I disorder
summary: Defined by at least one manic episode; depressive episodes are common but not required.

name: Bipolar II disorder
summary: At least one hypomanic and one major depressive episode, without a full manic episode.

name: Cyclothymic disorder
summary: Two or more years of numerous mood swings that fall short of full manic or depressive episodes.

name: Major depressive disorder
summary: Episodes of low mood or loss of interest, with changes in sleep, energy, appetite, concentration or self-worth.

name: Persistent depressive disorder
summary: A depressed mood lasting most days for two years or longer.

name: Premenstrual dysphoric disorder
summary: Marked mood and physical symptoms that arise in the premenstrual phase and ease soon after bleeding starts.

name: Disruptive mood dysregulation disorder
summary: Frequent severe temper outbursts and persistently irritable mood in children and adolescents.

name: Generalized anxiety disorder
summary: Excessive, hard-to-control worry about many things over at least six months.

name: Panic disorder
summary: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks followed by ongoing worry about more attacks or their consequences.

name: Social anxiety disorder
summary: Intense fear of social situations where others might judge you.

name: Agoraphobia
summary: Fear of places or situations where escape or help might feel unavailable.

name: Specific phobia
summary: Marked fear of a particular object or situation, out of proportion to the actual danger.

name: Separation anxiety disorder
summary: Excessive fear about separation from attachment figures, beyond what suits the person’s age.

name: Selective mutism
summary: Consistent failure to speak in particular social situations despite speaking elsewhere.

name: Obsessive-compulsive disorder
summary: Unwanted intrusive thoughts and repetitive behaviors or mental acts done to relieve distress.

name: Body dysmorphic disorder
summary: Preoccupation with perceived flaws in appearance that others barely notice.

name: Hoarding disorder
summary: Persistent difficulty discarding possessions, causing clutter that disrupts living spaces.

name: Trichotillomania
summary: Recurrent hair pulling that leads to hair loss, despite attempts to stop.

name: Excoriation disorder
summary: Recurrent skin picking that causes lesions, despite attempts to stop.

name: Posttraumatic stress disorder
summary: Lasting intrusion, avoidance, mood changes and heightened arousal after exposure to a traumatic event.

name: Acute stress disorder
summary: Trauma-related symptoms that appear within the first month after the event.

name: Adjustment disorders
summary: Emotional or behavioral symptoms in response to an identifiable stressor, out of proportion or impairing.

name: Reactive attachment disorder
summary: A pattern of emotionally withdrawn behavior toward caregivers, linked to severe neglect in early life.

name: Prolonged grief disorder
summary: Intense, persistent yearning or preoccupation after a death, lasting well beyond cultural norms.

name: Dissociative identity disorder
summary: Disruption of identity into two or more distinct states, with gaps in memory.

name: Dissociative amnesia
summary: Inability to recall important personal information, beyond ordinary forgetting.

name: Depersonalization/derealization disorder
summary: Persistent feelings of detachment from oneself or from the surroundings, with reality testing intact.

name: Somatic symptom disorder
summary: Distressing physical symptoms paired with excessive thoughts, feelings or behaviors about them.

name: Illness anxiety disorder
summary: Preoccupation with having or developing a serious illness, with few or mild symptoms.

name: Functional neurological symptom disorder
summary: Neurological-seeming symptoms, such as weakness or seizures, that don’t fit recognized neurological disease.

name: Anorexia nervosa
summary: Restricted intake, intense fear of weight gain, and a disturbed experience of body weight or shape.

name: Bulimia nervosa
summary: Recurrent binge eating followed by compensatory behaviors, with self-worth tied to shape and weight.

name: Binge-eating disorder
summary: Recurrent episodes of eating large amounts with a sense of lost control, without regular compensation.

name: Avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder
summary: Limited eating driven by sensory aversion, low interest or fear of consequences, not body image.

name: Insomnia disorder
summary: Ongoing trouble falling or staying asleep that causes daytime distress or impairment.

name: Narcolepsy
summary: Recurrent irrepressible sleep episodes, sometimes with sudden loss of muscle tone.

name: Nightmare disorder
summary: Repeated, vivid, distressing dreams that wake the person with clear recall.

name: Gender dysphoria
summary: Marked distress from a mismatch between experienced gender and gender assigned at birth.

name: Oppositional defiant disorder
summary: A recurring pattern of angry mood, argumentative behavior or vindictiveness, mainly toward authority figures.

name: Conduct disorder
summary: A repeated pattern of violating others’ rights or major age-appropriate rules.

name: Intermittent explosive disorder
summary: Recurrent impulsive outbursts of aggression that are out of proportion to the trigger.

name: Kleptomania
summary: Recurrent failure to resist urges to steal items not needed for use or value.

name: Alcohol use disorder
summary: A problematic pattern of alcohol use causing impairment or distress, with levels from mild to severe.

name: Opioid use disorder
summary: A problematic pattern of opioid use causing impairment or distress, with levels from mild to severe.

name: Gambling disorder
summary: Persistent, recurrent gambling behavior that causes significant problems.

name: Delirium
summary: An acute disturbance in attention and awareness that develops over hours to days and fluctuates.

name: Major neurocognitive disorder
summary: A significant decline in one or more areas of thinking that interferes with independence.

name: Paranoid personality disorder
summary: A pervasive distrust and suspicion of others’ motives.

name: Schizoid personality disorder
summary: A pervasive detachment from relationships and a narrow range of expressed emotion.

name: Schizotypal personality disorder
summary: Discomfort with close relationships, odd beliefs or perceptions, and eccentric behavior.

name: Antisocial personality disorder
summary: A pervasive pattern of disregard for and violation of others’ rights, beginning by age fifteen.

name: Borderline personality disorder
summary: Instability in relationships, self-image and emotion, with marked impulsivity.

name: Histrionic personality disorder
summary: Excessive emotionality and attention seeking.

name: Narcissistic personality disorder
summary: A pattern of grandiosity, need for admiration and low empathy.

name: Avoidant personality disorder
summary: Social inhibition, feelings of inadequacy and sensitivity to negative evaluation.

name: Dependent personality disorder
summary: An excessive need to be taken care of, leading to submissive and clinging behavior.

name: Obsessive-compulsive personality disorder
summary: A preoccupation with orderliness, perfectionism and control at the expense of flexibility.

name: Global developmental delay
summary: Delayed milestones in several areas of development in a child too young for standardized testing.

name: Language disorder
summary: Ongoing difficulty understanding or producing language that is below age expectations.

name: Speech sound disorder
summary: Persistent trouble producing speech sounds clearly enough to be understood.

name: Childhood-onset fluency disorder
summary: Stuttering: disruptions in the normal flow and timing of speech, starting in early development.

name: Social (pragmatic) communication disorder
summary: Difficulty with the social use of language and nonverbal communication, without the restricted patterns of autism.

name: Developmental coordination disorder
summary: Motor skills well below what’s expected for age, affecting daily activities.

name: Stereotypic movement disorder
summary: Repetitive, seemingly driven movements such as rocking or hand flapping that interfere with activities.

name: Persistent motor or vocal tic disorder
summary: Motor or vocal tics (not both) lasting more than a year.

name: Catatonia associated with another mental disorder
summary: A cluster of marked motor and behavioral signs such as stupor, mutism or posturing, tied to another condition.

name: Unspecified depressive disorder
summary: Depressive symptoms causing distress that don’t fit a specific depressive diagnosis.

name: Unspecified anxiety disorder
summary: Anxiety symptoms causing distress that don’t fit a specific anxiety diagnosis.

name: Disinhibited social engagement disorder
summary: Overly familiar behavior toward unfamiliar adults, linked to early social neglect.

name: Psychological factors affecting other medical conditions
summary: Psychological or behavioral factors that worsen the course or treatment of a medical condition.

name: Factitious disorder imposed on self
summary: Falsifying or inducing illness signs in oneself, without an obvious external reward.

name: Pica
summary: Ongoing eating of non-food substances in a way that’s inappropriate for development.

name: Rumination disorder
summary: Repeated regurgitation of food, which may be rechewed, reswallowed or spat out.

name: Enuresis
summary: Repeated passing of urine in bed or clothes in a child past the age of expected control.

name: Encopresis
summary: Repeated passing of stool in inappropriate places in a child past the age of expected control.

name: Obstructive sleep apnea hypopnea
summary: Repeated airway blockage during sleep that disrupts breathing and rest.

name: Restless legs syndrome
summary: An urge to move the legs, usually at rest or in the evening, relieved by movement.

name: Non-REM sleep arousal disorder, sleepwalking type
summary: Repeated episodes of rising and walking during sleep with limited awareness.

name: Non-REM sleep arousal disorder, sleep terror type
summary: Abrupt arousals from sleep with intense fear and little recall.

name: REM sleep behavior disorder
summary: Acting out dreams through movement or vocalization during REM sleep.

name: Erectile disorder
summary: Persistent difficulty getting or keeping an erection sufficient for sexual activity.

name: Premature (early) ejaculation
summary: Ejaculation that happens sooner than wanted, causing distress.

name: Delayed ejaculation
summary: Marked delay or inability to ejaculate despite adequate stimulation.

name: Female orgasmic disorder
summary: Marked delay, rarity or absence of orgasm, or much reduced intensity.

name: Female sexual interest/arousal disorder
summary: Reduced or absent sexual interest or arousal that causes distress.

name: Genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder
summary: Persistent pain, fear or tension tied to vaginal penetration.

name: Pyromania
summary: Repeated deliberate fire setting driven by tension and fascination rather than gain or anger.

name: Cannabis use disorder
summary: A problematic pattern of cannabis use causing impairment or distress, graded by severity.

name: Stimulant use disorder
summary: A problematic pattern of cocaine or amphetamine-type stimulant use causing impairment or distress.

name: Tobacco use disorder
summary: A problematic pattern of tobacco use with craving, tolerance or withdrawal.

name: Sedative, hypnotic or anxiolytic use disorder
summary: A problematic pattern of use of these medications causing impairment or distress.

name: Hallucinogen use disorder
summary: A problematic pattern of hallucinogen use causing impairment or distress.

name: Inhalant use disorder
summary: A problematic pattern of inhaling volatile substances causing impairment or distress.

name: Mild neurocognitive disorder
summary: A modest decline in thinking skills that doesn’t yet impair independence.

name: Major NCD due to Alzheimer’s disease
summary: Gradual decline in memory and other thinking skills attributed to Alzheimer’s disease.

name: Major NCD with Lewy bodies
summary: Cognitive decline with fluctuating alertness, visual hallucinations and parkinsonian features.

name: Major frontotemporal NCD
summary: Decline led by changes in behavior, personality or language.

name: Major vascular NCD
summary: Cognitive decline linked to cerebrovascular disease.

name: Personality change due to another medical condition
summary: A lasting change in personality caused by a medical condition.

name: Voyeuristic disorder
summary: Recurrent arousal from secretly observing an unsuspecting person, acted on or causing distress.

name: Exhibitionistic disorder
summary: Recurrent arousal from exposing oneself to an unsuspecting person, acted on or causing distress.

name: Frotteuristic disorder
summary: Recurrent arousal from touching or rubbing against a non-consenting person, acted on or causing distress.

name: Sexual masochism disorder
summary: Recurrent arousal from being humiliated, bound or made to suffer, causing distress or impairment.

name: Sexual sadism disorder
summary: Recurrent arousal from another’s suffering, acted on with a non-consenting person or causing distress.

name: Pedophilic disorder
summary: Recurrent arousal toward prepubertal children, acted on or causing marked distress. Needs specialist assessment.

name: Fetishistic disorder
summary: Recurrent arousal from nonliving objects or specific body parts, causing distress or impairment.

name: Transvestic disorder
summary: Recurrent arousal from cross-dressing, causing distress or impairment.

name: Other specified mental disorder
summary: Distressing symptoms that fit no specific category, with the clinician naming the reason.

name: Unspecified mental disorder
summary: Distressing symptoms where there isn’t enough information to be more specific.

name: Medication-induced acute dystonia
summary: Sudden sustained muscle contractions or abnormal postures after taking a medication.

name: Neuroleptic-induced parkinsonism
summary: Tremor, rigidity or slowed movement after antipsychotic or similar treatment.

name: Medication-induced acute akathisia
summary: Inner restlessness and an urge to move after taking a medication.

name: Tardive dyskinesia
summary: Involuntary movements, often of the face and tongue, after prolonged exposure to certain medications.

name: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome
summary: A rare, serious reaction to antipsychotics with fever, rigidity and altered awareness. A medical emergency.

room: Other conditions that may be a focus of clinical attention
name: Relationship distress with spouse or intimate partner
summary: Problems in a relationship that are a focus of clinical attention.

room: Other conditions that may be a focus of clinical attention
name: Uncomplicated bereavement
summary: Normal grief after a death that is a focus of clinical attention.

room: Other conditions that may be a focus of clinical attention
name: Phase of life problem
summary: Difficulty adjusting to a life transition.

room: Other conditions that may be a focus of clinical attention
name: Borderline intellectual functioning
summary: Intellectual functioning just above the range for intellectual disability.

room: Other conditions that may be a focus of clinical attention
name: Malingering
summary: Intentionally faking or exaggerating symptoms for an external reward.
